Open-weight models went from 7% to 56% of Vercel AI Gateway tokens in eight months. That is not a trend. That is a structural repricing of enterprise AI.

The Financial Times reports that open-weight models now handle 56% of Vercel's AI Gateway tokens as of August, up from 7% in December. AT&T runs 40% of its AI workloads on open-weight models and reports a 56% reduction in inference costs through cheaper routing. Coinbase reports approximately 50% savings from the same approach.

The executive implication is not about saving money — it is about what the savings enable. When inference costs drop by half, use cases that were economically unviable become standard operations. Internal AI workflows that required budget justification at frontier-model pricing become deployable at scale without incremental approval.

For CTOs, the architecture decision is now a portfolio question. The organizations gaining the most are not replacing frontier models entirely. They are routing intelligently — sending complex reasoning tasks to frontier models and high-volume commodity tasks to open-weight alternatives. The margin is in the routing logic, not the model choice.

For CEOs, this shift changes the competitive math. Your competitor is not necessarily spending more on AI. They may be spending the same amount but covering three times the operational surface area because their routing cuts inference costs in half.
